A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hierarchical sparse attention study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching retained content across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: V1 reports original BabiLong and RULER experiments, architectural and sparsity ablations, retrieval diagnostics, and RAMba experiments in Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds general-capability evaluation of an 8B MoE variant and decoding-latency measurements in Appendices A and E.

M1.justification: Appendix A introduces SWA-HSA-MoE with expert feed-forward blocks. The core chunk encoder, CLS token, bypass path, and retrieval procedure remain unchanged. Renaming DRT variants to SWA+HSA does not introduce per-token retrieval or stick-breaking weights; v1 already specifies both.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on MMLU, PIQA, BBH, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval+, and MBPP+. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained long-context retrieval and reasoning tasks to general knowledge, mathematics, and coding.

E2.justification: New Table 4 evaluates Transformer-MoE against SWA-HSA-MoE, and Table 7 compares RAMba latency with a full-attention Transformer and Mamba-2. Comparator membership in the retained BabiLong, RULER, and RAMba accuracy experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: The added MoE comparison uses matched 8B-total/1B-active models trained on 8T tokens with identical data mixtures and recipes. A separate timing protocol generates 100 tokens at batch size 16 with 4K, 16K, and 64K prompts, excluding prefilling. These substantially extend the evaluation design; existing experiments' settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E.2 adds a focused analysis of retrieval overhead and decoding-latency scaling with prompt length. The existing encoder, CLS, bypass, training-length, selection-sparsity, retrieval-frequency, and intermediate-retrieval analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. V2's added results continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Table 4 reports average scores of 57.69 for SWA-HSA-MoE versus 55.62 for Transformer-MoE, with gains on six tasks but lower MMLU. Table 7 adds latency results, including 2.76 seconds for RAMba versus 32.12 for the Transformer at 64K. Retained long-context results are unchanged, including 79.77% at 32M in Table 2.

T1.justification: Appendix E.1 adds computational-cost derivations for chunk encoding, selection, and selected-chunk attention, including cumulative selection cost O(L²d/C). This is a limited complexity supplement; the original RCA definition, attention-approximation reasoning, and residual equations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions, and conclusion retain the same architectural principles and training-free 4K-to-32M extrapolation claim. The new experiments supplement rather than redefine these headline contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations about preserving general capabilities at scale, possible information-filtering benefits for reasoning and coding, and modest computational overhead. Existing retrieval and integration explanations remain. The new universal-effectiveness language exceeds the demonstrated scope, which includes an MMLU decline and latency measurements only through 64K.

D1.justification: V2 adds a concrete code-repository address, specifies that MQ-N queries two of six key-value pairs, and documents the new MoE controls and timing procedure. Existing training recipes are retained. Detailed MoE implementation and data composition are deferred to Hu et al. (2025c), rather than supplied locally.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against SeerAttention and YOCO, plus citations to Every Token Counts and The Mamba in the Llama. It also clarifies the relationship between SWA+HSA and original DRT/GCA. Most other reference changes are bibliographic updates to already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 consistently adopts SWA+HSA terminology, expands the sparsity explanations, adds an experiments overview and Section 5.5, and reorganizes appendices around the additions. Affiliations, acknowledgements, and publication headers change. Most existing prose and the central narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds general-capability and latency tables, updates model labels in existing displays, and relocates or resizes architecture figures. Existing result-table structures and plotted findings are retained; appendix tables are renumbered to accommodate the additions.

improvement.justification: V2 provides useful evidence absent from v1 about general-task performance at larger scale and computational cost, while clarifying model terminology and code access. These gains are limited: the MoE study does not test extreme-length extrapolation, and timing excludes prefilling, stops at 64K, and does not directly measure SWA+HSA. Broad no-regression and deployment interpretations therefore remain insufficiently qualified.
